streaky-bay-17.name: Venus Bay Conservation Park
streaky-bay-17.bio: Cliffs, mangrove flats and beaches on the Weyland Peninsula, with an island tombolo and over 100 bird species.

notes.pin: Draft is Wikipedia's park point; park is large (Weyland Peninsula plus bay shore): pick a beach or day-use access near Venus Bay township.
notes.cost: Free entry per the park's own Fees page; camping fees only.

streaky-bay-18.name: South Head Walking Trail
streaky-bay-18.bio: A Venus Bay clifftop walk with the Needle Eye lookout, and dolphins, sea lions and, May to October, southern right whales.

notes.pin: Not yet located: midpoint of the trail at South Head, Venus Bay (start near Venus Bay township); tourism board lists it under Elliston office 21 Beach Terrace, Elliston.

streaky-bay-18.ticket_note: Walk is listed only on the regional tourism board page; no steward page found (council trail).

ceduna-1.name: Ceduna Jetty
ceduna-1.bio: A 380 m jetty on the Murat Bay foreshore with a swimming enclosure, whiting fishing and sunset views.

notes.pin: Jetty on Ceduna foreshore at Murat Bay, a short walk from the main street; use the jetty's mid-length point or its base.

ceduna-1.ticket_note: No single steward page found (council-run); regional tourism board page only.

ceduna-2.name: Pinky Point Lookout
ceduna-2.bio: A lookout at Thevenard with a telescope and signs, over the wharf, the channel and the Eleni K wreck offshore.

notes.pin: Thevenard end of the Encounter Walking Trail, Pinky Point; use the lookout platform.

ceduna-2.ticket_note: Listed only on the regional tourism board page.

ceduna-3.name: Laura Bay Conservation Park
ceduna-3.bio: A sheltered bay of mangroves and samphire flats where shorebirds feed, with a lookout and a 1911 grain landing.

notes.pin: Draft is Wikipedia's park point; use the park's lookout or the headland landing site.
notes.cost: Vehicle entry free; fees apply only for camping.

ceduna-4.name: Acraman Creek Conservation Park
ceduna-4.bio: Mangroves and dunes by the Great Australian Bight, for canoeing, fishing and watching migratory waders.

notes.pin: Draft is Wikipedia's park point; no designated visitor point found: use Port Lindsay or the creek launch if located.
notes.cost: Entry free; fees for camping only; camp sites must be booked.

ceduna-5.name: Smoky Bay
ceduna-5.bio: An oyster-farming village on Smoky Bay with a swimming-enclosure jetty and oyster farm tours.

notes.pin: Draft is Wikipedia's town point; the jetty near the boat ramp is the visitor point.
notes.cost: Village and jetty free. Oyster Deck Experience tours (Sandy Creek Drive, ph 04 2825 7177) are a separate paid operator; no price found, so not applied to this spot.

ceduna-5.ticket_note: Village with no single steward; the oyster tour operator's site oysterdeckexperience.com.au could not be reached by script.

ceduna-6.name: Point Bell Conservation Park
ceduna-6.bio: A rocky point of granite boulders, long beaches and dunes for fishing, swimming and camping, reached by 4WD only.

notes.pin: Draft is Wikipedia's park point; 8 unallocated 4WD-only campsites, no designated trails; use the headland/beach access.
notes.cost: Entry free; fees for camping only.

ceduna-7.name: Penong Windmill Museum
ceduna-7.bio: An outdoor museum of about 20 restored windmills, including Bruce, the largest in Australia, beside the highway.

notes.pin: Beside Highway 1 at Penong, 71 km west of Ceduna; point to be found by the pin pass.

ceduna-7.ticket_note: Only the regional tourism board page found; the museum's own site was unreachable by script.

ceduna-8.name: Cactus Beach
ceduna-8.bio: A remote surf beach 21 km south of Penong with two left-hand and one right-hand break.

notes.pin: Draft is Wikipedia's coordinates for the beach itself; surf breaks sit on the west side of Point Sinclair.
notes.note: Tourism board URL in the draft returned 404; surf-break facts from Wikipedia. Camping at Point Sinclair is not verified.

ceduna-8.ticket_note: No steward page found; tourism board URL for it returns 404.

ceduna-9.name: Lake MacDonnell
ceduna-9.bio: A pink salt lake off Point Sinclair Road south of Penong, coloured by salt-loving algae, with green and blue lakes beside it.

notes.pin: Wikipedia's lake point (centroid); visitor stop is the causeway on Point Sinclair Road about 15 km south of Penong.
notes.rename: Draft 'Lake Macdonnell' renamed to Wikipedia's spelling 'Lake MacDonnell', which therefore needs no wiki field.

ceduna-9.ticket_note: No steward; regional tourism board page only.

destination.name: Ceduna
destination.tagline: Oyster farms and surf breaks at the last big town before the Nullarbor.
destination.description: Ceduna sits on Murat Bay on the Eyre Highway, the last major town before the Nullarbor. A 380 m jetty runs out from its foreshore, and the oyster farms of Smoky Bay lie 45 km along the coast. To the west, Penong has a roadside windmill museum, and the road south leads to the surf breaks of Cactus Beach and the salt lakes beside it. Conservation parks with mangroves and shorebird feeding grounds line the coast either side of town.
whyVisit: Eat fresh oysters from the farms

goodToKnow.title: Check the fire danger
goodToKnow.detail: Conservation parks here close on days of Catastrophic fire danger and may close on Extreme days, so check the CFS rating before you go.

goodToKnow.title: 4WD for Point Bell
goodToKnow.detail: Point Bell is reachable by four-wheel drive only, and west coast beach driving can be treacherous. Lower tyre pressures on sand.

destination.bestTimeBlurb: {months} are mild enough for coastal walks and the long Eyre Highway drive.
